method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

Automated screening compared source references, locators, geography fields, evidence class, direction, status, horizon and scenario; it checked pathway support IDs, link-evidence sets, geography fields, alternatives and uncertainty for follow-up.

Raw extraction access rows are recorded only as inherited access observations. This generated screen does not treat snippets, HTTP success, prior access, or metadata as claim verification and does not replace semantic source review.

evidence.compact_statement: Bhutan's mountainous setting, reliance on hydropower and agriculture, and limited resources and capacity shape its climate vulnerability.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: National climate response and 12th Five-Year Plan discussion, printed pp. 3-4 (PDF pp. 3-4).

evidence.compact_statement: The NDC reports that the 12th Five-Year Plan includes climate resilience and disaster preparedness priorities and describes national coordination arrangements for climate action.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The assessment identifies glacial lake outburst floods, flash floods, landslides, forest fires, and windstorms alongside slower-onset glacial retreat and ecosystem degradation, with implications for water, food, energy, infrastructure, health, and livelihoods.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: October 2025 event case study, printed p. 79 (PDF p. 92).

evidence.compact_statement: The report records heavy rain on 4-5 October 2025 followed by flash floods, landslides, swollen rivers, and windstorms; it notes crop, livestock, home, cultural-site, infrastructure, and hydropower impacts, one death, and two people missing, with Samtse, Chukha, Haa, and Dagana among the most affected districts.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Climate risk and economic impact summary, webpage paragraphs on climate scenarios and projected losses (accessed 2026-10-26).

evidence.scenario: Hotter-and-drier scenario described in the official summary; no named model pathway is specified there.
evidence.compact_statement: The World Bank release says hotter and drier conditions could affect hydropower, tourism, and agriculture and produce economic losses by 2050; it reports that adaptation and diversification could reduce projected losses by at least 40 percent.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Climate risks for communities and locations, webpage paragraphs on population and subnational exposure (accessed 2026-10-26).

evidence.compact_statement: The release reports that about 65 percent of Bhutan's population is exposed to at least one natural hazard and identifies Zhemgang and Mongar among districts with higher risk; floods, landslides, and heat disproportionately affect vulnerable people.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The 2022 vulnerability assessment's present-risk index ranks Samtse, Monggar, Sarpang, Punakha and Dagana highest using older administrative indicators; not a 2026 risk or loss ranking.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The 2022 assessment gives Zhemgang, Dagana and Gasa the lowest adaptive-capacity index scores; slower recovery is an inference, not measured outcomes.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.
